newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot power prices steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot power prices steady to higher.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the Midwestern U.S. were steady to higher Monday with expectations of some heating demand due to colder weather driving prices higher, industry sources said.
"We have some cold weather coming in, and power out of Canada is getting a little more expensive due to some cold and snow up there," said one Mid-West power marketer.
With the exception of the east and west coastlines, much of the U.S. was forecast to have below or much-below temperatures from October 24 to 28.

In the East Central Area Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak, non-firm electricity prices for Tuesday delivery were said to be holding relatively steady at $17.00-19.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
Peak electricity for the five business days of next week was also assessed steady at $17.00-19.50 per MWh.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was talked steady in the $12.50-14.00 area, the sources said.
November ECAR prices held at $17.25-17.55, while December was pegged steady near $18.70-19.10.

Peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) region were talked higher at $15.50-16.50 from Monday delivery quotes at $15.00-16.00 late last week, the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power was also assessed higher at $9.00-11.00 per MWh from $8.00-10.00 late last week.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), non-firm peak power for Tuesday delivery was said to be steady to higher at $16.50-19.00 from a Monday delivery range of $16.50-18.00, the sources said.
Off-peak next day MAIN power was pegged steady in the $11.50-13.00 range.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak, non-firm power for Tuesday delivery was assessed higher at $21.00-25.00 from last week quotes for Monday delivery at $19.00-20.00 for the entire region, the sources said.
Next-day power in SPP was said to have been buoyed by the expected cooler weather and the outage of two Entergy units.
Entergy delayed startup of its 836 megawatt Arkansas nuclear power unit 1 until Thursday from original restart estimates set for this past weekend.
Also, Entergy's 1,173 megawatt Grand Gulf nuclear power unit 1 was taken off line over the weekend as expected for maintenance and refueling that was scheduled to last through to late November.
Off-peak prices in SPP held steady in the $12.00-14.00 area, the sources said.
November SPP was discussed steady at $18.50-19.25, while December SPP was talked in the $22.25-22.50 range for the southern area of the region, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
